correctness.rationale: The formula holds for distinct spins in the stated β=1, zero-field normalization. In the frozen method the Stirling factor and sextic entropy term give g(x)=x²/2−x⁶/30 for W=M/N^{3/4}; normalized ratios, not bare weights, give the coefficient Cov(W²,g)=−a²/5. Quartic tails are negligible outside the growing central window; full-lattice integration of smooth quartic-weighted polynomials has error O(h²) on either lattice translate by a second-derivative bound, h=2N^{-3/4}, which is smaller than the required O(N^-1) for the scaled moment. Exchangeability subtracts the N diagonal terms exactly. An independent continuous calculation gives the same answer: Gaussian decoupling makes the spins conditionally independent with conditional mean tanh t and mixing density proportional to exp[−N(t²/2−log cosh t)]. Thus c_N=E tanh²t. For t=N^-1/4 x the mixing law expands against exp(−x⁴/12) with relative correction N^-1/2 x⁶/45; tanh²t=N^-1/2 x²−(2/3)N^-1x⁴+O(N^-3/2 x⁶). The potential is bounded below by a positive multiple of t⁴ near zero, has its unique global minimum at zero and grows quadratically at infinity, allowing termwise normalized integration with the claimed remainder. The coefficient is (μ₈−μ₂μ₆)/45−2μ₄/3=−(1+a²/5) using μ₂=a, μ₄=3, μ₆=9a, μ₈=45.
residual_risks: The numerical frozen check is corroborative only. No claim is made outside the exact critical zero-field model or for coincident sites.

originality.rationale: Already covered as a direct moment consequence of Can and Pham (2017), not merely of the leading quartic limit. In exactly the same model, Theorem 1.4 prints the normalized first distribution correction using p₂(t)=(t²/2−t⁶/30)e^{−t⁴/12}. Crucially, their proof in §§3.2–3.3 gives the pointwise central expansion with an integrable polynomial times the quartic weight at order O(N^-1), as well as an exponentially small outer sum. Multiply that expansion by x² for the numerator and use it unweighted for the denominator. Summing the weighted remainder still gives relative O(N^-1); the grid spacing is 2N^-3/4 and the whole-line quadrature for each displayed smooth term costs O(N^-3/2) after multiplication by the spacing. Normalizing gives E[W²]=a+N^-1/2[(μ₄−a²)/2−(μ₈−aμ₆)/30]+O(N^-1)=a−N^-1/2a²/5+O(N^-1). The exact identity c_N=(√N E[W²]−1)/(N−1) now gives the frozen coefficient and remainder. It is immaterial that the source chooses a distribution tail, rather than a distinct-spin pair, as its named statistic: the very same local expansion and error control already settle this moment.
residual_risks: This review does not identify the earliest possible occurrence; the 1978 paper and other earlier critical-moment treatments could also bear on priority.
Can–Pham's proof supplies the expansion used here; this review does not assert that their paper prints the pair coefficient as a displayed formula.

value.rationale: Critical pair dependence and the susceptibility correction are natural observables, and the formula is useful as a concise corollary or reference calculation. But the frozen record's proposed new narrow exact fact is mechanically implied by the published correction profile and its established remainder. Applying the second-moment observable and subtracting the known diagonal contribution offers no surviving independent exact invariant, new regime or structural extension. No repair is warranted on the available result.
residual_risks: The failure concerns research contribution, not the coefficient's correctness or usefulness in an expository note crediting the prior derivation.
